assertions.interpretation: The main event: Su Jun's eastern campaign against Shen Chong.
During the campaign, Su Jun invited Lu Mai, the Clerk of the Ministry of Personnel, to accompany him.

assertions.exact_span: 將至吳密勑左右令入閶門放火以示威
assertions.interpretation: As they were about to reach Wu, Su Jun secretly ordered his attendants to enter the Chang Gate and set fire to display power.
assertions.surface: 將至吳密勑左右令入閶門放火以示威

assertions.exact_span: 陸知其意謂峻曰吳治平未久必將有亂
assertions.interpretation: Lu Mai perceived Su Jun's intent and warned that Wu had not been pacified for long and would surely have disorder.
assertions.surface: 陸知其意謂峻曰吳治平未久必將有亂

assertions.interpretation: As a result, Su Jun stopped his plan to set fire.

assertions.exact_span: 諂事王敦敦克京邑以充爲車騎將
assertions.interpretation: Background: Shen Chong had previously flattered and served Wang Dun; when Wang Dun conquered the capital, he made Chong a chariot-and-cavalry general.
assertions.surface: 諂事王敦敦克京邑以充爲車騎將

assertions.exact_span: 充字士居吳興人少好兵
assertions.interpretation: Background: Shen Chong's courtesy name was Shiju, a native of Wuxing, fond of military affairs from youth.
assertions.surface: 充字士居吳興人少好兵

assertions.exact_span: 男兒不建豹尾不復歸矣
assertions.interpretation: Quoted speech: Shen Chong declared he would not return unless he established a leopard-tail banner (i.e., achieved high military rank).
assertions.surface: 男兒不建豹尾不復歸矣

assertions.exact_span: 領吳國内史明帝伐王敦充率衆就王舍
assertions.interpretation: Background: Shen Chong held the post of Governor of Wu; when Emperor Ming campaigned against Wang Dun, Chong led his troops to join Wang She.
assertions.surface: 領吳國内史明帝伐王敦充率衆就王舍

assertion.interpretation: Lu Mai proposed that if disorder were to begin, it should start from his own household.

assertion.exact_span: 敦死充將吳儒斬首於軍
assertion.interpretation: Later outcome: After Wang Dun died, Shen Chong's general Wu Ru beheaded him in the army.
assertion.surface: 敦死充將吳儒斬首於軍

assertion.exact_span: 陸碑曰邁字功高吳郡人噐識清敏風檢澄峻累遷振威
assertion.interpretation: Background from Lu's stele: Lu Mai's courtesy name was Gonggao, a man of Wu Commandery, of clear and keen discernment, who was repeatedly promoted to Zhenwei (general).
assertion.surface: 陸碑曰邁字功高吳郡人噐識清敏風檢澄峻累遷振威
